intro: If you have errands in Mahachai town, you're keeping watch over a patient at Samut Sakhon Hospital, or you just want a roomy, clean place to stay a while at a budget price — Thongchen Residence is a 3-star serviced apartment-hotel in a high-rise on Soi Ekkachai 11, right in central Mahachai and next to Samut Sakhon Hospital. It takes both daily and monthly stays and is open 24 hours. Rooms are freshly fitted and spacious, with air-con, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, and many with a city-view balcony. body.html: The main draw of Thongchen Residence is that it's a roomy apartment-hotel taking both daily and monthly stays right in central Mahachai — an area where fresh, clean rooms you can settle into for a while at a budget price aren't easy to find. The building sits on Soi Ekkachai 11, right next to Samut Sakhon Hospital, within walking reach, which makes it a natural pick for people keeping watch over a patient, visiting relatives, medical staff on a temporary posting, or anyone moving into town for work who needs a place for several nights.

Because it was designed as a place to actually live in, the rooms here are more spacious than a typical hotel room at the same price. There's a choice from Studio and Studio with Balcony to Standard Twin and Family rooms. Every room has air-con, a large fridge, a flat-screen TV, a desk and a private bathroom, and many have a city-view balcony. Real guest reviews often praise the rooms as fresh and clean, the fittings still looking new, comfortable beds and strong air-con.

What guests praise most is the convenient, good-value central location. It's right by Samut Sakhon Hospital, with restaurants, convenience stores, fresh markets and government offices all around, so it's easy to get about on foot. There's free parking, a lift, an in-house cafe, and Wi-Fi that several reviews call strong and reliable. It's open and staffed around the clock with CCTV covering the building, so a late check-in or a night arrival is no problem.

"Spacious, clean room, fittings still new, a big fridge, cold air-con and strong Wi-Fi, right next to the hospital — really handy for keeping watch over a patient, and good value for both daily and monthly stays."

The main thing to set expectations for is that the in-room supplies are fairly basic — not stocked like a full-service hotel. Some reviews mention only one roll of toilet paper, no soap, no hairdryer, and no kettle in certain rooms. Extra pillows can come at a charge. If you're staying several nights or by the month, it's worth bringing your own toiletries, since this is run as an apartment rather than a hotel that restocks daily.

Another point guests raise is that shower water pressure in some rooms is on the weak side, so a wash takes a little longer. One review mentioned a smell from the bathroom drain, which can be sorted by asking to change rooms or flagging it to the front desk. The room style is plain and modern rather than flashy, so anyone after a resort-style feel may find it spare — but for those who value a big, clean room and a good location, that's rarely an issue.

Overall, Thongchen Residence scores around 8.2 out of 10 from real guest reviews, roughly 12 of them, and ranks near the top of its property type in Samut Sakhon. It's a roomy apartment-hotel that suits people keeping watch over a patient at Samut Sakhon Hospital, workers needing several nights, or anyone after a budget monthly stay in the town centre. Rates start around ฿750 for a Studio and climb to roughly ฿900–1,200 for larger or family rooms, with monthly rates working out even better per night. If you can accept the basic in-room supplies and the water pressure, it's a good-value pick in central Mahachai.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Thongchen Residence, Samut Sakhon

faq.q: Where is Thongchen Residence and what's nearby?
faq.a: Thongchen Residence is at 1500/119 Soi Ekkachai 11, Ekkachai Road, Mahachai, Mueang Samut Sakhon. It's in central Mahachai, right next to Samut Sakhon Hospital and walkable to it, near the Mueang Mai fresh market and Mahachai Market, and about a 7–8 minute drive from Mahachai railway station and CentralPlaza Mahachai.

faq.q: How much does Thongchen Residence cost and can I stay monthly?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿750/night for a Studio. Larger and family rooms climb to roughly ฿900–1,200 depending on dates and room type. It takes both daily and monthly stays — if you're here several nights, ask for the monthly rate, which works out far better per night. Always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Thongchen Residence good for keeping watch over a patient at Samut Sakhon Hospital?
faq.a: Very much so, because it's right next to Samut Sakhon Hospital and walkable. It's open 24 hours with staff and CCTV around the building, so late check-ins are fine. Rooms are spacious with a large fridge and free parking, making it handy for relatives staying several nights.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Thongchen Residence — are supplies provided?
faq.a: Rooms are fresh, spacious and clean, with air-con, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, and many with a city-view balcony. But in-room supplies are basic — some reviews note minimal toilet paper, no soap/hairdryer, and no kettle in certain rooms — so it's worth bringing your own toiletries, especially for a longer stay.

faq.q: Does Thongchen Residence have parking and a lift?
faq.a: Yes — there's free parking and a lift. There's also an in-house cafe, free Wi-Fi that reviews call strong, and CCTV around the building. It suits self-drivers and anyone who wants a roomy, secure place to stay in central Mahachai.

faq.q: What downsides should I know about before booking Thongchen Residence?
faq.a: Things to note are that shower water pressure in some rooms is weak, and one review mentioned a smell from the bathroom drain, which can be sorted by changing rooms. Supplies are basic and extra pillows can incur a charge. The room style is plain and modern rather than resort-like, but the focus is a big, clean room and a good location at a fair price.
